summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and end-stage renal disease status post renal transplant was admitted for hypertensive urgency, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. He had been unable to take his oral medications due to gastrointestinal symptoms, leading to severely elevated blood pressure. He was initially managed in the ICU with intravenous antihypertensives and then transitioned to oral therapy. Renal ultrasound revealed new-onset renal artery stenosis, contributing to his hypertension and graft dysfunction. A tunneled hemodialysis catheter was placed on hospital day 1, and he began hemodialysis on day 2, completing three sessions with good tolerance. His nausea improved with dialysis. Medication changes included discontinuation of CellCept and Lasix, continuation of tacrolimus and prednisone, uptitration of doxazosin, and transition of calcitriol and epogen to in-center administration. He was discharged home in stable condition with a plan for ongoing outpatient dialysis and follow-up.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, malignant, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
